tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Hyperbolization of a simplex with deleted vertices] 1. 13.5.4\group tetrahedra Source: thurston:page-0346, thurston:page-0347

Let $O$ be an $n$-orbifold with the combinatorial type of an $n$-simplex from which some vertices have been deleted. If every deleted vertex has a Euclidean orbifold as its link and the Coxeter diagram of $O$ is connected, then $O$ admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure.
Proof

\sketch A deleted vertex gives a rank-$(n-1)$ principal submatrix of the face Gram matrix. In a basis adapted to its null vector, connectedness of the Coxeter diagram makes the remaining coupling nonzero, so the full matrix has signature $(n,1)$. The other principal submatrices are positive definite or rank-$(n-1)$ semidefinite, placing every vertex in hyperbolic space or on its ideal boundary. The resulting simplex is therefore complete and has finite volume.
